planned_outcome: Land HMS Hermione: leave-one-sensor-out cross-validation diagnostic on M9 Stefan and M12 Zurcher fits, plus sensor calibration-floor measurement at t=0 across 7 fixtures. Determine whether the 6-22 deg C in-sample main-bake RMSE was sensor-side noise/calibration or genuine model misfit. If LOO-RMSE on held-out sensor is below 2 deg C, the verdict revises to GO (Method 3 viable); if matches in-sample, CONFIRM-information-limit stands.
actual_outcome: LOO cross-validation diagnostic complete. Calibration floor: median sigma 0.11 deg C, range 0.34 deg C — sensor noise definitively NOT the cause of 6-22 deg C model residual (12-44x noise floor). Zurcher 5-param LOO: 35/35 fits with held-out RMSE > 4 deg C; median 18.3 deg C; max 37.2 deg C. Stefan PDE LOO: 12/15 above 4 deg C; median 6.4 deg C. Surface-side held-out sensors fit well (T5 BA3C 1.9, T3 wonder_white 1.9); deep held-out sensors fail (T1 wonder_white 21.0). Model captures field near BC, fails far from it. Verdict CONFIRM-information-limit: M7-M12 in-sample RMSE was genuine missing-physics model misfit, not sensor-side noise. The data is informative near the surface and uninformative near (and past) the probe tip — exactly the opposite of what x_core extrapolation needs.
success_metric_result: Calibration floor 0.11 deg C; Zurcher 0/35 LOO fits under 2 deg C; Stefan 2/15 LOO fits under 2 deg C; verdict consistent across both model classes.

adopt: LOO cross-validation is the gold-standard test for inverse-problem viability — it distinguishes overfitting (LOO >> in-sample) from genuine model adequacy (LOO close to in-sample). Should be standard for any future physics-inversion work
avoid: Treating in-sample RMSE as evidence of model adequacy; always run LOO before declaring an inverse problem successful
